name: Johan H. Andresen
current_role: Chairman of the Board, Ferd AS (Oslo)
profile: Fifth-generation head of the Andresen family business (Tiedemanns tobacco, bought 1849), which he renamed Ferd in 2001 and turned into a Nordic investment group (Elopak, Aibel, Swix, real estate, funds). CEO 1998-2012, chairman since 2012; in 2007 he passed most shares to daughters Katharina and Alexandra, and in Dec 2023 said his A-shares will go to a Ferd Foundation.
interesting_fact: In 2006 he bid about NOK 11 billion for Swiss packaging maker SIG to merge it with Elopak, which would have made the world's No. 2 packaging group; he dropped the bid in 2007 after a bidding war.
deep_cut_fact: Before joining the family business he worked as a product manager at International Paper in the US (1989-91). In 2009 he founded Ferd Social Entrepreneurs, and he helped launch the Norwegian Microfinance Initiative (2008). He has also chaired the Council on Ethics for Norway's Government Pension Fund Global.
notes: Dropped the 'Jr.' from his name after his father died in 2011. Ferd's 2023 annual report lists Ferd JHA AS (100% his) as a shareholder alongside his daughters' holding companies. For an energy angle, Ferd co-owns the oil-services firm Aibel.

name: Nirmal Kumar Minda
current_role: Chairman (Executive Chairman), UNO Minda Ltd; President of ASSOCHAM for 2025
profile: Second-generation head of UNO Minda (formerly Minda Industries), a Gurugram-based maker of auto switches, lighting, alloy wheels and EV components. He joined his father Shadilal's business in 1977 and ran it on his own after a 1996 split with his brother. He built it through Japanese and European joint ventures and moved from MD to Chairman in April 2025.
interesting_fact: The business goes back to 1958, when his father Shadilal Minda started importing ammeters from Japan. It moved to Delhi in 1962 to serve the tractor and motorcycle aftermarket.
deep_cut_fact: The group's first joint venture (1995) came from a quality push by Maruti. Minda asked the carmaker to help find a Japanese partner for switches, which led to Toyota-group supplier Tokai Rika. Separately, he and his wife Suman run Samarth-Jyoti, which operates two schools, a 100-bed hospital and 18 village centres.
notes: The Samarth-Jyoti detail comes from an India CSR profile (https://indiacsr.in/biography-nirmal-kumar-minda-president-assocham-2025/). EV components and ASSOCHAM policy work are possible podcast angles. Sources differ on his exact title (Chairman vs Chairman & MD).

name: Edward J. DeBartolo, Jr.
current_role: Founder and CEO, DeBartolo Holdings LLC (Tampa, FL)
profile: Son of mall pioneer Edward J. DeBartolo Sr. He joined the family's Edward J. DeBartolo Corp. in 1971 and led its 1996 merger with Simon Property Group. He owned the San Francisco 49ers from 1977 to 2000, a stretch that brought five Super Bowl titles. Since 2002 he has run DeBartolo Holdings, which covers real estate development, private equity investments, sports and philanthropy.
interesting_fact: Inducted into the Pro Football Hall of Fame in 2016 as a contributor. Steve Young credited his 'family approach', which treated players as partners, with changing how NFL owners run teams.
deep_cut_fact: In 2007 he co-founded Brooks-DeBartolo Collegiate High School in Tampa with Hall of Fame linebacker Derrick Brooks. At the 2014 flag-football game that was Candlestick Park's last football event, Joe Montana threw him the final touchdown pass.
notes: No published email. DeBartolo Holdings lists a main office line, 813.908.8400, at its Tampa HQ (debartoloholdings.com contact section). Avoid his 1998 Edwin Edwards case and the 2020 pardon. Debartolo.com is a parked domain, not his.

name: Jonathan Nelson
current_role: Founder and Executive Chairman, Providence Equity Partners
profile: Jonathan M. Nelson (Brown '77) co-founded Providence Equity Partners in Providence, RI in 1989. It has since backed more than 180 media, communications, education and information companies. Wins include selling PADI in 2017 for over $700M and roughly sextupling a $300M 2007 stake in ZeniMax when Microsoft bought it for $7.5B. He is now executive chairman and a trustee of Rockefeller University.
interesting_fact: In college he worked at a commercial radio station, hosting the 'Jazz After Hours' program. Today he sits on the board of the Newport Festival Foundation, which runs the Newport Folk and Jazz Festivals.
deep_cut_fact: In 2016 his $25 million gift created the Jonathan M. Nelson Center for Entrepreneurship at his alma mater, Brown. He had earlier funded Brown's Nelson Fitness Center, and he serves as a Fellow of the Brown Corporation.

public_contacts.value: Pro-Providence@profileadvisors.com (Profile Advisors, listed as Providence Equity media contact)

notes: Media enquiries go through the PR firm Profile Advisors. The Brown entrepreneurship center and his jazz/Newport interests make good outreach hooks. Providence invests in communications infrastructure, which is relevant to data centers.

name: Shi Jiazhang
current_role: Chairman, Chi Mei Corporation (since May 2026); also Director of the Chi Mei Museum and Chairman of Chi Mei Culture Foundation
profile: Hsu Chia-chang (許家彰), 62, is the only son of Chi Mei founder Shi Wen-long (許文龍). Chi Mei, based in Tainan, Taiwan, is the world's largest ABS resin maker. He has chaired Chi Mei's appliance arm (CHIMEI/新視代) since 2010 and joined the group board in 2013. In May 2026 he succeeded his father's cousin Hsu Chun-hua as chairman, pledging a shift from volume to high-spec medical, semiconductor and auto materials.
interesting_fact: On taking over, he summed up his strategy as moving Chi Mei 'from quantity to quality' and building a 'green value chain', in response to a glut of Chinese petrochemical capacity.
deep_cut_fact: As a boy he was made to practise the violin every day by his father, who built the Chi Mei Museum's famous violin collection. He has called that childhood 'torment' a lifelong spiritual asset. He now directs the museum himself.

public_contacts.value: cmm@chimeimuseum.org (Chi Mei Museum, which he directs)

notes: The name in the input is a pinyin rendering; he is usually written Hsu Chia-chang (許家彰). Media-shy, he gave a rare interview to Mirror Media (鏡週刊) in mid-2026. Chi Mei's contact page is JavaScript-rendered, so no corporate press email was captured. Specialty materials for semiconductors are a possible podcast angle.

name: Maritsa Lazari
current_role: Co-founder and Director, Lazari Investments (London); trustee, Christos Lazari Foundation
profile: Born in Dora, Cyprus in 1943, she moved to London at 16 and married fellow Cypriot Christos (Chris) Lazari in 1965. In 1978 the couple put profits from his Drendie Girl fashion label into London property. Lazari Investments now owns over 3M sq ft, mostly West End offices plus the Brunswick Centre. Since Chris died in 2015 she has stayed on as a director alongside their three children.
interesting_fact: The fortune began with a high-street fashion label: Chris saved money from washing dishes and waiting tables to study fashion design, and Drendie Girl funded the move into property in 1978.
deep_cut_fact: The family's Christos Lazari Foundation, set up in 2017 with Maritsa as trustee, supports Cypriot, Greek Orthodox and medical causes. It gave £3.25m of investment property to the Cypriot children's charity Radiomarathon.
notes: Very private, with almost no interviews on record. The foundation's published email is the only route found. Lazari Investments has no verified official website (lazari.co.uk sits behind a bot wall and could not be confirmed). Her sons are also directors. Little obvious energy or data-center fit beyond London office property.

name: Prasert Prasarttong-Osoth
profile: Died 21 April 2026, aged 93. He was a former surgeon who co-founded Bangkok Dusit Medical Services in 1972 and founded Bangkok Airways. Son Puttipong now leads the airline and daughter Poramaporn is president of BDMS.
notes: Deceased (21 Apr 2026), per Khaosod English and Nation Thailand (https://www.nationthailand.com/news/general/40065318). Profile skipped as per the instructions. For BDMS or Bangkok Airways, contact the next generation instead.

name: Devi Prasad Shetty
current_role: Founder and Chairman, Narayana Health (Narayana Hrudayalaya Ltd), Bengaluru
profile: Cardiac surgeon from Karnataka, trained at Kasturba Medical College and Guy's Hospital, London. He founded Narayana Hrudayalaya in Bengaluru in 2001 and grew it into a listed hospital chain, including a facility in the Cayman Islands, built on assembly-line economies of scale. That model has pushed bypass surgery prices to a fraction of US costs, and his family holds a majority stake.
interesting_fact: The Wall Street Journal called him 'the Henry Ford of heart surgery'. His hospitals save money with tricks like cross-ventilation instead of air-conditioning, and their surgeons do 30-35 operations a day.
deep_cut_fact: He grew up the eighth of nine children in Kinnigoli village and chose heart surgery as a schoolboy after hearing of Christiaan Barnard's first heart transplant. In 1992 in Kolkata he performed India's first neonatal heart surgery, on a 21-day-old baby. He also co-designed Yeshasvini, Karnataka's low-cost farmers' health insurance scheme.
notes: Padma Shri (2004) and Padma Bhushan (2012). He speaks often about healthcare economics and frugal innovation, which suits an entrepreneurship podcast. No dedicated press email was found; investor relations is the best published route.

name: Stephen Deckoff
current_role: Founder and Managing Principal, Black Diamond Capital Management (also director and 10%+ holder of KVH Industries)
profile: Distressed-credit and private-equity investor who worked at Drexel Burnham Lambert, Chemical Securities, Bear Stearns and Kidder, Peabody (SVP) before founding Black Diamond in 1995. The firm now manages more than $11B across CLOs, distressed funds and control private equity, with holdings including Werner ladders and Polynt. He has lived in the US Virgin Islands since 2011, where the firm has an office.
interesting_fact: He is an avid skier and named Black Diamond Capital after the ski-slope rating for the hardest runs.
deep_cut_fact: He studied operations research, earning a B.S. from Cornell's engineering school, and has sat on the boards of an unusually varied set of portfolio companies, including Werner Ladder, SmarteCarte, Sun World, Bayou Steel and ION Media.
notes: No published email or press contact; the firm site lists only office addresses (Stamford CT, St. Thomas USVI, Mumbai). In 2023 he bought Little and Great St. James islands (formerly Epstein's) for a resort, which is widely covered but sensitive, so avoid it as an opener. Reported >$1.2M in USVI nonprofit donations (St. John Source). Industrial portfolio (steel, paper, chemicals) may suit the energy angle.
